title: Compact segment coalescer and TTL-aware inline cache for dashboard query API
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Several dashboard endpoints used by the Console 'Usage Explorer' experience exhibit large variance in tail latency under mixed workloads. Root causes identified: high read-amplification on the primary time-series index, many small range scans for tenant/time windows, and redundant recomputation of prefix aggregates for adjacent pages. Goal: reduce 95th/99th percentile query latency by 35% for paginated exploration flows while cutting average datastore read units by 40% for heavy tenants.
background: Usage analytics queries frequently request contiguous time ranges with small page sizes (10-50 rows) but many adjacent cursors across sessions. Our current approach issues multiple overlapping range scans and relies on a best-effort application cache which invalidates broadly on any write. Existing tickets touched related areas (ENG-34912, ENG-62188) but we need a targeted runtime-level coalescing and TTL-aware inline cache to eliminate redundant scans without increasing staleness beyond acceptable bounds.
proposed_solution: 1) Implement a compact segment coalescer in the Console backend that merges adjacent range queries within a short window (200ms) into a single wider scan and slices results per-original-cursor. 2) Add a TTL-aware inline cache keyed by (tenant_id, route, canonicalized-time-window, aggregation-version) with per-route invalidation policies and soft-TTL that favors serving slightly-stale cached prefixes for interactive pagination. 3) Introduce a small in-memory priority prefetch queue to warm next-page segments for active sessions using an LRU that is shard-aware to avoid cross-shard amplification.
design_details:
- Coalescer: front-door component on query fan-in that groups queries with overlapping time ranges and compatible sort keys. Use deterministic slice mapping so tracing and quotas attribute correctly. Back-pressure limits: max coalesced span = 30s or 5x requested span, whichever is smaller.  
- Inline cache: store compressed segment payloads with metadata: start_ts, end_ts, aggregations_hash, inserted_at, ttl_seconds. Cache lookup falls back if aggregation_version mismatch. Soft-TTL default = 30s; hard TTL = 5m. Support explicit invalidation for routes that are eventually consistent.  
- Prefetch queue: per-tenant bounded queue that promotes next-page ranges when client has sequential cursor access pattern. Priority weights favor low-latency routes and recent activity.  
- Metrics: instrument coalescer hit/miss, cache hit ratio by tenant/route, average scan width after coalescing, extra tokens saved, and prefetch usefulness (fraction of prefetches used).  
- Storage considerations: cache entries stored in backend process memory with metrics and fallback to Redis for larger tenants; segmented eviction policy tuned per-tenant quota.
tasks: Spike: microbenchmark coalescer behavior with synthetic overlapping queries (2d)
Design review: API surface and tracing changes (1d)
Implement coalescer and deterministic slicer in query-router (4d)
Implement TTL-aware inline cache with per-route policy (3d)
Implement priority prefetch queue and tenant-aware limits (2d)
End-to-end tests: correctness, staleness bounds, concurrency (2d)
Load test against production-like trace replay (3d)
Deploy canary with 5/25/100 rollout plan and monitoring dashboards (1d)
Post-rollout review and perf regression guardrails (1d)
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency for Usage Explorer paginated endpoints reduced by >= 35% compared to baseline
Average datastore read units consumed per heavy-tenant exploration reduced by >= 40%
Cache hit ratio >= 60% for sequential pagination patterns on canary tenants
No data-consistency regressions: documented staleness profile is within soft-TTL bounds and validated by test harness
Tracing shows coalesced queries are correctly attributed to original cursors and quotas preserved
rollout_plan: Canary stage 1: 5% of traffic (internal tenants) for 24h, observe latency and error budget
Canary stage 2: 25% of traffic (selected production tenants across regions) for 48h
Full rollout: ramp to 100% with monitoring alarms enabled; automatic rollback policy on error budget breach or >10% increase in 99th latency
Post-rollout: run 72h stability window and schedule a retro
monitoring_and_alerting: Add panels: coalescer_coalesced_queries/sec, inline_cache_hit_ratio (per-route), avg_scan_span_seconds, prefetch_use_rate, datastore_read_units_by_tenant. Alerts: cache_hit_ratio < 30% for a tenant AND increase in read units > 25% => rollback; P99 latency increase >10% for 15m => immediate rollback. Link these to PagerDuty channel 'console-performance'.
notes: Tradeoffs: serving slightly stale pages improves interactive latency but may confuse cross-session comparisons; we need clear UX messaging on last-updated for affected widgets.
We considered a distributed read-through cache (Redis-only) but initial microbenchmarks showed unacceptable network overhead for small segment sizes; hybrid in-memory + Redis chosen.
Kernel-level datastore optimizations might further reduce read amplification but are out of scope for this ticket and tracked separately.
